call_points.text: NIM improved to 3.17% in Q2FY27 from 2.72% a year ago.
Management guides 15-20% advances growth and 10-15% liabilities growth, for about 15% overall business growth.
ROA target raised to 1.35-1.40% from "1% plus", after Q1FY27 ROA of 1.29%.
NIM improved to 3.20% from 3.07% in Q4FY26 and 2.82% in Q1FY26; management expects further improvement.
Cost of funds fell 22 bps QoQ to 5.16%, helped by shifting bulk deposits to retail term deposits.
CD ratio rose to 78.45% from 76.61% in March and 71.93% a year ago; management wants it higher.
SMA-2 rose to ₹750 Cr from ₹635 Cr; management said it does not foresee additional provisioning from slippage.
On the ECL mandate, management said it is ready and does not foresee a problem.
Employee cost is expected to stay in the same range next quarter onwards.
On the MD & CEO tenure extension, management called it a process and pointed to exchange filings.
Q4 NIM at 3.07%, up from 2.92% in Q3, driven by RAM-segment yield and CASA improvement; management sees NIM bottomed out.
Management admits retail and MSME growth has lagged and says retail growth will take time.

operating_notes.text: Deposits rose to ₹1,08,777.07 Cr at Mar-2026 from ₹1,04,806.20 Cr a year earlier; advances rose to ₹81,809.63 Cr from ₹76,541.48 Cr.
Proposed dividend of ₹189.09 Cr not appropriated from FY26 profit; reckoned in capital adequacy computation.
Bank allotted 2,44,900 equity shares during FY26 under the Employee Stock Options Scheme.
Q4FY26 credit cost was 0.1% and slippage 0.20%, down from 0.11% and 0.47% in Q3FY26.
IBPC and food credit book cut to ₹1,707 Cr at Mar-2026 from ₹4,057 Cr a year earlier, with ₹2,350 Cr replaced by higher-yielding loans.
Technically written-off portfolio is about ₹2,500 Cr, with management targeting 50% recovery.
Partnered with the Tobacco Board of India to provide specialized financial solutions and timely credit to registered tobacco growers in Karnataka.
Enabled seamless EPF payments in EPFO portal via Internet Banking integration.
IBPC portfolio cut to ₹1,375 Cr as of June 2026 from ₹1,618 Cr in March 2026, with ₹243 Cr replaced by higher-yielding loans.
Retail term deposits below ₹3 Cr grew 3% QoQ to ₹69,410 Cr; bulk deposits were 4.7% of total deposits.
Retail book was ₹48,622 Cr, mid-corporate ₹16,636 Cr and large corporate ₹21,352 Cr as of June 2026.
PCR stood at 85.78% as at September 30, 2026, compared to 81.05% as at September 30, 2025.
Total deposits reached ₹1,15,117.15 Cr and gross advances stood at ₹90,581.25 Cr as of September 30, 2026.

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (consolidated): interest earned ₹2,257.32 Cr (-0.1% YoY), net profit ₹408.25 Cr (+61.6% YoY).
Karnataka Bank released its Q4FY26 investor presentation showcasing an 8% QoQ increase in gross advances and a PAT of ₹408.19 Cr.
Karnataka Bank's Q4FY26 earnings call (May 20, 2026) guided FY27 advances growth of 15-20% and ROA above 1%, after FY26 GNPA fell to 2.78% and NNPA to 0.98%.
On June 1, 2026, Karnataka Bank reported on its Annual Conference of Concurrent Auditors and Internal Auditors held on May 20, 2026.
On June 2, 2026, Karnataka Bank announced its partnership with the Tobacco Board of India to offer specialized financial solutions to registered tobacco growers.
On June 3, 2026, Karnataka Bank announced the integration of its Internet Banking with the EPFO portal for digital PF payments.
Karnataka Bank unveiled 'Nava Dhamaka 2026', a suite of nine digital and retail banking solutions.
Q2FY27 results (consolidated): interest earned ₹2,503.87 Cr (+14.9% YoY), net profit ₹435.86 Cr (+36.5% YoY).
On October 28, 2026, The Karnataka Bank released its investor presentation for Q2FY27, reporting a 36.6% YoY jump in PAT to ₹435.89 Cr.
The Karnataka Bank Limited disclosed the audio recording of its post earnings analysts/institutional investors conference call held on 29 October 2026 at 04:00 PM IST.

status_history.evidence: GNPA fell to 2.78% at Mar-2026 from 3.32% at Dec-2025, beating the sub-3% guidance.

watchlist.text: Shareholder approval of ₹5 final dividend at the ensuing AGM

watchlist.response: Management said it was difficult to answer and gave no number, citing yield and business expansion uncertainty.
watchlist.text: Analysts repeatedly asked for FY27 employee cost guidance after a sharp Q4 decline.

watchlist.response: CFO said the information would be shared later by email, as it was not available on the call.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked for the G-Sec and EBLR mix of the loan book and the gratuity impact on employee cost.

watchlist.response: Management said it could not answer and did not have the figure at hand.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked for the interest reversal benefit from lower Q4 slippages.

status_history.evidence: ROA reported at 1.26% in Q2FY27 vs 1.29% in Q1FY27.

watchlist.response: Management said the rise was partly due to holidays around 30 June and that it does not foresee additional provisioning from slippage.
watchlist.text: SMA-2 rose to ₹750 Cr from ₹635 Cr in a quarter with the lowest provisions, suggesting higher provisioning ahead.

watchlist.response: Management said only that efforts will continue to drive continuous improvement, without specifying.
watchlist.text: Whether the 1.35-1.40% ROA aim is an exit run-rate or the full-year average.

watchlist.response: Management called it a process and referred investors to stock exchange filings, without giving a timeline.
